title: Stop Loss & Take Profit
hook: Protect your capital first. Always know your exit before your entry.

launchpad.outcome: Place a stop loss based on structure, not comfort.
launchpad.missionQuestion: In an uptrend, does your stop loss belong at a comfortable distance, or at the point that proves the setup wrong?

slides.headline: Your stop goes where you’re wrong.
slides.line: Not some random number of points away. Not wherever feels comfortable.

slides.kicker: Where does the stop actually belong?
slides.headline: Tap the point that proves this uptrend wrong.

tool.kicker: Where does the stop actually belong?
tool.title: Tap the point that proves this uptrend wrong
tool.intro: Your stop loss belongs where the setup is proven wrong, not some random number of points away, and not just wherever feels comfortable.

rounds.prompt: This is an uptrend with one pullback so far. Where does the stop loss actually belong?

points.feedback: Exactly. That's below the swing low, the point where this uptrend idea is actually proven wrong. A close beneath it means the structure failed.
That's just a comfortable distance from current price, it isn't tied to the point where the trade idea is actually proven wrong.

slides.headline: Price is closing in on your stop.
slides.line: It pulls back close, without closing below the swing low.

check.prompt: Should the stop move closer to “reduce risk”?

options.label: Yes, tightening it feels safer
options.feedback: Tightening a stop based on fear usually gets you stopped out of a trade that was still valid.

options.label: No, that abandons the invalidation point
options.why: Right. Your stop protects the plan. Moving it out of fear defeats its purpose.

slides.line: It protects your account and your structure logic, and it isn’t about ego.

slides.headline: A stop only works if you respect it.

check.prompt: After entry, discipline means you ___ to the plan instead of moving your stop out of fear.

options.label: React
options.feedback: Reacting is exactly what fear-based stop-moving is, the opposite of sticking to the plan.

options.label: Guess
options.feedback: The plan already answered this, no guessing needed.

options.label: Stick
options.why: Committing to the plan is what makes a stop loss actually work.

slides.prompt: Why can’t you just move your stop when a trade goes against you?
slides.modelAnswer: Your stop is placed at the point where the trade idea is actually proven wrong, moving it out of fear just delays finding that out, and usually costs more in the end. If you move your stop every time you’re scared, it isn’t protecting anything anymore; it’s just following your emotions instead of your plan.

takeaways: A stop loss belongs where the setup is actually proven wrong, not wherever feels comfortable.
Moving your stop out of fear defeats the reason it exists.
A take profit is planned in advance, not decided in the moment.
remember: Your stop protects the plan, not your feelings in the moment.
